To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a strong relationship between the similarity of augmentations and corruption robustness in feature space, (2) augmentations can be perceptually similar to ImageNet-C, and (3) augmentations that are dissimilar from ImageNET-C can hurt corruption robustness

(1) we introduce a novel feature space for image transformations, (2) we show that the Minimal Sample Distance between data augmentation and test corruption is correlated with performance, (3) we show that recent augmentations may risk being overfitted to the existing benchmark by being perceptually dissimilar to the corruptions.

(a) there is a strong relationship between the perceptual similarity between data augmentations, test-time corruptions, and corruption robustness; and (b) augmentations can overfit to the existing benchmark of test-time corruptions and degrade corruption robustness when sampled to be dissimilar to the benchmark

the similarity in feature space between augmentations (training) and corruptions (test) matters.

augmentations and corruption robustness can interact in complex ways, and that it is important to consider the perceptual similarity of augmentations to the corruption benchmark when developing data augmentations for corruption robustness.
